study.question: Can eight explicit same-field target-query versus action-pool dot products improve the frozen incumbent, where raw action-pool vectors and backward-path controls regressed, beyond equal-capacity amplitude-only and history-projection readouts?
study.hypothesis: A provisional limitation is the format of the extra semantic readout, rather than only shared-gradient interference: the shallow classifier may not recover useful target/pool products from raw vector concatenation under the fixed recipe. Exposing signed target/pool interactions as eight scalars may preserve complementary coarse relevance. This is a local implementation hypothesis, not evidence of a measured representation bottleneck or a new dot-product invention.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit task-adapted embeddings, target-aware relevance and MLP. DIN already uses products in local activation and discusses pooling intensity. New local change exposes eight pooled same-field query/value dot products to the classifier; it does not reproduce DIN normalization or claim to invent interactions.

Adopt only the explicit candidate/history interaction readout idea. Here there are two coarse fields, four actions, one uniform-null pool per field/action and eight scalar features entering the existing shallow classifier. No per-layer highway, dual bus, token-mixing backbone, new supervision or optimizer. Source tiny-mode ablations and different label/split do not establish transfer. The inspected classifier section4.5 also appends uncompressed cross-dot Gram features alongside compressed bus tokens. Our eight query/action-pool products are a coarse, single-stage adaptation, not a first proposal of compression plus interaction readout.

Only the author field warning is verified: no historical item identity is available. Full publisher text remains unavailable. Use category/brand/action/age only and make no DMR reproduction or comprehensive priority claim.

study.proposed_difference: Append eight zero-initialized first-layer columns after the complete incumbent. For each category/brand and action, let q=existing same-field target+0.5*blind-static-context query and p=sum(valid field/action values)/(n+2). Candidate scalar=<q,p>/sqrt(16); magnitude replacement=norm(q)*norm(p)/sqrt(16); projection replacement=sum_coordinates(p)/sqrt(16). All three arms compute identical tables and select only the final eight scalars; no additional learned modules or random draws. Missing target, missing history field and empty action produce exactly zero. Shared gradients remain live in all arms. Product, magnitude and projection are readout replacements, not simultaneous interacting interventions.
predictions: Primary: relevance_dot exceeds the incumbent full-population validation AUC and both matched readout controls. Its advantage should have the same direction on paired seeds43,44 before repeated support is claimed. A gain over only the incumbent is insufficient attribution.

The history_gt64 slice (3026583 samples,151372 positives,2875211 negatives) dominates previous regressions. Predeclare its AUC difference as a secondary directional check; inspect all fixed host slices with counts and no multiplicity-based significance claim.

Source and host diagnostics should show unchanged parent prefix, finite B logits, zero unsupported extras, dot bounded in absolute value by the magnitude readout, and nonzero fitted extra-column use. Fixed-checkpoint feature replacements measure dependence only.

Dot versus magnitude tests directional interaction beyond vector amplitude; dot versus projection tests target interaction beyond a fixed eight-scalar compression. Raw128 comparisons are contextual evidence only, not matched proof of readout format.

If magnitude or projection matches/exceeds dot across paired seeds, signed target/pool alignment is not supported as the source of any improvement.
If seed42 advantage reverses or disappears at43/44, report preliminary or null evidence; do not infer mechanism from one run or a slice selected after inspection.
Nonfinite outputs, unsupported/missing-target leakage, changed parent prefix/RNG, or parameter mismatch invalidate execution attribution and require repair within the charged budget.
Near-zero fitted extra use or identical replacements suggests redundancy; nonzero sensitivity alone does not establish utility.
alternative_explanations: Eight-scalar compression can regularize relative to128 raw coordinates; matched projection control addresses only one fixed compression, not all learned projections.

Magnitude-only nonnegative and signed dot/projection have different distributions and backward derivatives. A dot gain could reflect optimization/scale, not semantic relevance. No calibration sweep is proposed.
Queries include inherited blind context and pooled values include action/age embeddings, so an effect is not uniquely pure category/brand similarity.
All arms use shared live embeddings; gradients, norm growth and implicit regularization remain part of the treatment. The r0041 backward factorial did not isolate a general explanation.
Historical best-of-many selection and repeated reuse of validation create selection bias. No unseen test, per-user predictions or independent bootstrap interface is available here.
Fixed-history truncation, undocumented static snapshot dates, coarse hashed fields and absence of historical item IDs limit causal and production claims.
